AI agents are no longer just generating code snippets—they are running local SSH authentication and handling 567 Git pushes per second.

Here are the top AI engineering updates from the past 24 hours:

🛠️ Reason Machines open-sourced Aspen, a self-hosted Git server built for AI agents. Based on OpenAI’s Pando design, internal testing demonstrated it can sustain 567 pushes per second on a single 8-core server.

📄 Google AI introduced the Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin to bring a spec-first approach to automated coding. Under this architecture, coding agents draft software specs and run through 5 zero-context review stages before writing any actual code.

🔐 ChatGPT Desktop now supports forwarding your local SSH agent to remote machines. This enables the remote agent to authenticate using your local credentials and push directly to your private GitHub repositories.

🍏 Apple is accelerating work to make Siri more agentic. CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI head Craig Federighi to fast-track the roadmap so Siri can compete directly with agent products like OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse.

⚠️ Nvidia launched an official investigation into CEO Jensen Huang following an employee memo acknowledging an affair with Alice Huang, an AI executive and agent of the Chinese government.

With agents taking on tasks like running spec reviews and authenticating over SSH, developer tooling is evolving rapidly toward full autonomy.

How is your team handling security controls as AI agents gain access to local credentials and repositories?
